record.paper_title: Open Problems in α Particle Condensation
record.original_question: For infinite α matter made of freely moving α particles, what first-principles calculation with full antisymmetrization of the nucleon wave function can determine the low-density symmetric-matter energy per nucleon, the α-pair distribution function, and the density-dependent modification of the α form factor?

evidence.quote: The full calculation for α matter (freely moving α particles) would give the energy per nucleon for symmetric matter in the low-density limit. Furthermore, it would be of importance to calculate the α-pair distribution function in infinite matter, and to calculate the modification of the α form factor at increasing nucleon density within such a first principle approach that includes the full antisymmetrization of the nucleon wave function.

artifact.status_search_result: No published first-principles, fully antisymmetrized ab initio calculation of infinite α matter delivering simultaneously the low-density energy per nucleon, the α–α pair distribution function, and the density dependence of the in-medium α form factor was located. Related work treats α–α effective interactions or finite α-cluster nuclei, but the infinite-matter program with full nucleon antisymmetrization remains a stated open task.

status_evidence.title: Nucleon-alpha potentials - ScienceDirect
status_evidence.snippet: The nucleon-alpha potential is calculated using a microscopic model with antisymmetrisation effects included.
status_evidence.claim: Microscopic antisymmetrized treatments exist for finite nucleon–α systems but not for the infinite α-matter problem with the three observables requested.

status_evidence.title: Effect of quark antisymmetrization on binding energy of nuclear matter
status_evidence.snippet: Antisymmetrization effects on binding energy per nucleon in nuclear matter are estimated via linked cluster expansion.
status_evidence.claim: Existing antisymmetrization-in-matter studies focus on uniform nuclear matter, not on α-clustered infinite matter with form-factor and pair-distribution outputs.
